edition.internalStatus: HY-1.0 LIVE · gate 20/20 PASS · revision #28 held (10/8/72/10) · quiet 0/10.

views.client: Stocks fell sharply at the open and then recovered most of the loss: the S&P 500 dropped as much as 3.2% before closing down 0.25%, the Nasdaq fell 0.6% and the Dow rose 0.3%. Core inflation for October came in at 3.3%, slightly above forecasts, and a December rate rise remains almost fully priced. Treasury yields still fell. Oil rose after an attack on a Saudi oil terminal, with WTI at $83.68 and Brent at $94.61. Our reading stays DISINFLATION / HAWKISH PIVOT; two of four conditions are met.
views.internal: The market took a hot core inflation print and a 3% morning plunge and closed nearly flat, with the equal-weight index up and yields down. That is not panic. But the S&P now sits below the line where we call the trend broken, and the break comes from the largest technology names, not from the rest of the market. Oil is moving the other way: Brent is $0.39 from $95 after the Ras Tanura attack.

drivers.t: Hot core PCE, AI sell-off, recovery
drivers.b: Core PCE 3.3% (vs 3.2%). S&P −3.2% at the low, −0.25% at the close; Nvidia −3.9%; equal-weight +108bp ahead of the cap-weighted index; yields lower.

drivers.t: Oil up on Saudi terminal attack
drivers.b: January WTI 83.68 (+1.63), reference 84.88; Brent 94.61 (+3.21) after four drones were intercepted over Ras Tanura.
